title: Research
text: I built and validated a full genomic prediction pipeline for puberty and fertility traits (reproductive tract score, pelvic height/width, days open, heifer pregnancy) across five beef cattle breed populations — Angus, Red Angus, Hereford, a Bos indicus-influenced population, and a pooled MultiBreed population of over 9,000 animals genotyped on an 800K SNP panel. The pipeline spans univariate, bivariate, and multi-trait single-step GBLUP and GBLUP models via BLUPF90+/GIBBSF90+, with genetic parameter estimation (heritability, genetic correlations) via REML/AI-REML and prediction accuracy validated using the LR (Legarra & Reverter, 2018) temporal validation framework. Related work includes a Breed-As-Trait analysis estimating genetic correlations for the same traits measured across different breeds, and a population-stratification-adjusted (PCA-corrected) extension of the MultiBreed models.

title: Research
section: Cross-species, evidence-informed genomic prediction in legumes
text:
Cross-species, evidence-informed genomic prediction in legumes
Building on a systematic RNA-seq meta-analysis of common bean stress transcriptomes (19 public datasets, machine learning and network-based gene discovery), I evaluated whether SNP subsets prioritized by proximity to biologically evidenced stress-responsive genes improve genomic prediction accuracy relative to standard equal-weight GBLUP and random-marker controls. This framework has been applied to bacterial wilt and soybean cyst nematode resistance in common bean, and — via cross-species ortholog mapping — to abiotic stress tolerance (drought, salt) in cowpea.

title: Research
text:
Disease resistance breeding and genetics
My earlier graduate and industry work focused on plant pathology and disease-resistance breeding directly: breeding spinach for resistance to the downy mildew pathogen Peronospora effusa, including genetic characterization of resistance loci and race-specific resistance across worldwide germplasm, and three years evaluating field corn, sweet corn, and soybean for pathogen resistance within Syngenta’s Trait Assessment pipeline.

title: Dotun Olaoye
text:
I am a PhD candidate in Statistical Genetics at the University of Missouri, Columbia, working with Dr. Jared Decker in the Genetics Area Program. My research centers on quantitative genetics and genomic prediction, spanning both animal and plant breeding systems: multi-breed genomic evaluation of puberty and fertility traits in beef cattle, and cross-species genomic prediction of disease-resistance and abiotic-stress traits in legume crops (cowpea, common bean).
Before my PhD, I completed a Master of Science in Plant Breeding, Genetics and Pathology at the University of Arkansas, where I worked on breeding spinach for resistance to the downy mildew pathogen Peronospora effusa, and spent three years as a Pathology Research Specialist at Syngenta Seeds Inc., evaluating field corn, sweet corn, and soybean for disease resistance within a commercial trait-advancement pipeline. My academic foundation is in plant pathology, from a Bachelor of Agriculture (Honors: Crop Protection/Pathology) at the Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta, Nigeria.
Across these roles, my work has combined statistical genetics methodology — single-step GBLUP, mixed-model genetic evaluation, LR validation — with hands-on plant pathology and breeding experience, applied to problems in both livestock and crop improvement.
